evals.prompt: Record our decision to use PostgreSQL rather than DynamoDB as the billing service's primary datastore. Context: billing needs multi-row ACID transactions and complex relational reporting queries, and the team is fluent in SQL. Options we weighed: PostgreSQL on RDS, DynamoDB, and MySQL on RDS. Decision: PostgreSQL on RDS. Consequences: we own schema migrations and eventually hit vertical-scaling limits, but we get transactional integrity and rich querying today.
evals.expected_output: The decision is consequential and non-obvious with all required parts supplied, so the skill writes a new ADR at docs/adr/0001-*.md (zero-padded to four digits, kebab-cased title), with Status Accepted, today's date, and the four default sections filled from the request, and creates a docs/adr/README.md index linking to it.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run evals/files/setup_new.sh (a plain project with no ADR directory). Invoke the skill there.
expectations: Exactly one ADR file is created, at docs/adr/, and no ADR directory pre-existed so it defaults to docs/adr.
The filename is 0001-<kebab-title>.md — zero-padded to four digits, title kebab-cased (e.g. docs/adr/0001-use-postgresql-for-billing.md).
The ADR contains a `- Status: Accepted` line (the decision is presented as final, not proposed).
The `- Date:` line equals today's date in YYYY-MM-DD form (the output of `date +%F`), not a guessed or hallucinated date.
The ADR has the four default sections in order: `## Context and drivers`, `## Considered options`, `## Decision`, `## Consequences`.
The Considered options section lists at least two options (PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, MySQL) drawn from the request, not invented.
The Decision section records PostgreSQL on RDS as the chosen option.
A docs/adr/README.md index is created with a table row linking the ADR number to its file.
No content is fabricated beyond what the request supplied (judgement).

evals.prompt: Record an architecture decision: we're consolidating our six service repos into a single monorepo. Context: duplicated CI config across repos and cross-repo changes are painful to coordinate atomically. Options considered: keep polyrepo with shared tooling, monorepo managed with Nx, monorepo managed with Bazel. Decision: monorepo managed with Nx. Consequences: one CI pipeline and atomic cross-service commits, at the cost of larger clones and a stronger need for code-ownership rules.
evals.expected_output: The skill discovers the existing doc/adr directory (not the default docs/adr), and matches its conventions: numbers the new ADR 008 with three digits, mirrors the existing section headings, writes it into doc/adr, and appends a row to the existing doc/adr/README.md index rather than creating a new one.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run evals/files/setup_existing.sh (a project with doc/adr/007-use-a-rest-api.md using three-digit numbering and a non-default section layout, plus an index). Invoke the skill there.
expectations: The new ADR is written into the existing doc/adr directory — no new docs/adr directory is created.
The new file is numbered 008 with three digits (matching the existing 007 width), e.g. doc/adr/008-adopt-a-monorepo.md — not 0008 and not restarting at 001.
The new ADR mirrors the existing file's section headings (Context / Decision Drivers / Considered Options / Decision Outcome), not the skill's own default section names.
The title line follows the existing style (e.g. `# 8. Adopt a monorepo`).
The considered options include the three supplied options (polyrepo, Nx monorepo, Bazel monorepo).
A row for the new ADR is appended to the existing doc/adr/README.md; the 007 row is preserved and no second index file is created.
The pre-existing 007 ADR is left unchanged (judgement).

evals.prompt: Write an ADR documenting that we've decided to use the date-fns library for date formatting on the frontend.
evals.expected_output: The decision is a routine, easily-reversible library pick with no architectural weight, so it fails the consequential-and-non-obvious bar. The skill declines to write an ADR, explains why, and creates no file (optionally asking the user to confirm if they still want one).
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run evals/files/setup_new.sh (a plain project with no ADR directory). Invoke the skill there.
expectations: No ADR file is created and no docs/adr (or other ADR) directory is created.
The skill explains the decision does not meet the bar — it is easily reversible / obvious / a routine library choice — rather than silently writing one.
The skill either stops or asks the user whether they really want an ADR, instead of defaulting to writing one (judgement).
No options, rationale, or consequences are invented to pad out a record (judgement).

evals.prompt: We've decided to move the public API from REST to GraphQL — this supersedes ADR 0001. Context: clients over-fetch and need flexible field selection across many screens. Options considered: keep REST with sparse fieldsets, adopt GraphQL via Apollo Server, adopt gRPC-web. Decision: adopt GraphQL via Apollo Server. Consequences: a new schema and resolver layer to own plus a team learning curve, but flexible queries and fewer round-trips.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes a new ADR (0002) whose Decision names that it supersedes 0001, flips ADR 0001's status to Superseded-by-0002, and updates both rows in the index.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run evals/files/setup_supersede.sh (a project with an accepted docs/adr/0001-use-a-rest-api.md and an index). Invoke the skill there.
expectations: A new ADR docs/adr/0002-*.md is created (four-digit number, matching the existing 0001 width) for the GraphQL decision.
The new ADR's Decision (or body) explicitly states it supersedes ADR 0001.
The existing 0001 file's status line is changed to reflect it is superseded by 0002 (e.g. `- Status: Superseded-by-0002`).
The docs/adr/README.md index is updated: the 0001 row shows the superseded status and a row for 0002 is added.
The new ADR uses the same section layout as the existing 0001 (Context and drivers / Considered options / Decision / Consequences).
The considered options include the three supplied options (REST with sparse fieldsets, GraphQL, gRPC-web).

evals.prompt: ADR 0003 has been accepted by the team — please update its status.
evals.expected_output: A pure status change: the skill flips ADR 0003 from Proposed to Accepted and updates its index row, without creating any new ADR file or altering the rest of the record.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run evals/files/setup_status.sh (a project with docs/adr/0003-adopt-event-sourcing.md in Proposed status and an index). Invoke the skill there.
expectations: No new ADR file is created — the directory still contains exactly one ADR (0003).
The `- Status:` line of docs/adr/0003-adopt-event-sourcing.md is changed from `Proposed` to `Accepted`.
The Status row for 0003 in docs/adr/README.md is updated to Accepted.
No other content of the 0003 ADR (context, options, decision, consequences, date) is modified (judgement).
The skill does not invent a new decision or ask for options/consequences it does not need for a status change (judgement).
